limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

Prerequisite records and some supporting actions used the acting or other staff role's API session: record creation, team changes, the competing expiry write, archiving before the C18 and C19 read-only checks, and the extra Tasks and Key dates for the ordering and Next deadline checks. The actions each article instructs were done in the browser.
The partial-save case used a reviewer route that answered one comment POST with 503; it proves the dialog's handling, not a real storage outage.
Reminder email delivery and timing were not exercised; notifications.md owns those rules. Only the saved lead times and recipient selection were checked.
The shared work lab also carried other agents' records; list, Home and calendar checks searched for this run's own DOC-029 contracts-b records.
The technical source review is recorded in docs/documentation/batches/DOC-029/contracts-b/technical-review.json.
The renewal checks used fictional term dates in 2026 and 2027; the passed-date banner used an expiry 5 days before the run date.

I replayed the round 1 V-C18 (term fields, derived Key dates, Renew dialog routes, stale and competing confirmations, banner, archived refusal) walkthrough for Legal Team Member and Administrator on lab openlaw-docs-41255c61-work2 built from 57e77e38, and every step passed. From 57e77e38 to 432dba3a, round 3 found only apps/web/src/routes/welcome.tsx and its test changed. The wizard now goes to /auth/two-factor/enroll after it saves a policy that requires two-factor authentication. The article makes no statement about the setup wizard Authentication step or two-factor enrollment. The change touches only apps/web/src/routes/welcome.tsx and its test, so no statement in the article can become wrong.
